text:
jordan: Quick proposal: policy compiler emits tiny, versioned "hints" (p95/p99 targets, cost cap, preferred regions). adapters can optionally consume hints and return ranked candidates.

sam: Why not put the SLA logic in policy?

jordan: Runtime latency is sensitive. If adapters can score locally against precomputed profiles, we cut a network hop and decision time. Policy still owns intent.

lee: Two immediate concerns: reproducibility and explosion of adapter behavior. We need a strict, minimal adapter response contract.

nora: Suggested response shape: `{candidates:[{id:"ded-1",score:0.79,uncertainty:0.22,reason:"p99 ok"}],profile_id:"ps-2026-03-18",cid:"c-123"}`. Keep it tiny.

sam: Uncertainty is key. How computed?
jordan: Start simple: use probe sample variance + sample size heuristic. Document exact formula in RFC appendix.

lee: Rollout plan idea: compiler emits hints in manifests (no runtime change) -> adapters read hints in sim-only mode and write parity logs -> run sims over production traces -> canary enable hinted-mode for few tenants with double-check against legacy router -> flip if telemetry gates pass.

nora: Telemetry gates: decision drift < 4%, p99 regressions < 5%, cost increase < 6%. Also monitor uncertainty histogram.

sam: Edge cases: cold starts, warmpool priming, and tail spikes. Adapters should add `stale:true` or `cannot_score` when profiles are old. Runtime falls back to legacy router in that case.

lee: Security: hints live in control plane only. Encrypted at rest and removed from user-facing logs. Rationale should be derivable from policy source for audits.

jordan: Dev tasks: RFC appendix for hint schema + uncertainty semantics (I can draft), sim harness changes (Lee), adapter shim prototype (Sam), ops dashboard + alerts (Nora).

ops-bot: created ticket #ops/route-hints-canary and calendar invite for adapter-hints-sync (30m)

jordan: Cool. 48h RFC draft window, then a 30m sync. Thumbs?

sam: +1
